interpretation: Private three-round validation medians 26–85% lower, including 21.6% lower for 4 MiB table payload. Normalization 16–56.5% lower. These exclude rendering, RPC, fixture construction and hashing.

Two final full-frame-verified 20-trial repeats: 4 MiB table acknowledgement medians 2.82% and 3.25% lower; edit-to-applied medians 2.06% and 2.41% lower. Each trial sums eight individual edits; applied observation includes projected RPC, scheduling and Python/socket overhead.
Small-console edit-to-applied medians vary -4.45%/-0.08%; 64 KiB table -3.01%/-4.53%. Do not generalize isolated validation gains to overall UI speed.
Unchanged runtime API controls vary -7.1% to +1.9%; unchanged cron match microcontrol -5.5%. Retained as variation/code-layout observations, not attributable improvements.
Native executable 2,902,800 to 2,886,288 bytes (-16,512, about 0.57%). Allocation counts, peak memory, RSS, cold startup and native Linux performance were not measured.
No universal Bash superiority, model performance or production-completeness claim. Generic UI transport/validation only; application control flow remains in .program.
